title: Adaptive DCS-SOMP for Localization Parameter Estimation in 5G Networks
subtitle: Core Argument Coverage Plan: From 3D Channel Modeling to Adaptive Sensing Matrix Optimization

nodes.title: Problem Definition: Limitations of Existing 2D and Coarse Estimation Methods
nodes.purpose: Identify the gap in current literature where methods either restrict estimation to 2D environments, fail to estimate all key parameters (ToA, 2D-AoD, 2D-AoA), or require additional refinement steps like SAGE.

nodes.title: System Model: 3D MIMO-mmWave Channel with UCA
nodes.purpose: Define the physical layer assumptions, including the use of Uniform Circular Arrays (UCA) to enable 2D angle estimation (azimuth and elevation) and the mathematical formulation of the channel matrix H[n] incorporating ToA and angular parameters.

nodes.title: Sensing Matrix Construction: Kronecker Product and Candidate Grids
nodes.purpose: Explain the construction of the initial sensing matrix ω(0) using response vectors for all possible azimuth/elevation combinations, highlighting the dependency on candidate counts (qaz, qel) and the resulting memory complexity.

nodes.title: Core Mechanism: Dynamic Adaptive Search Space Reduction
nodes.purpose: Detail the proposed adaptive algorithm that iteratively narrows the search interval for angles based on previous iteration results, allowing high resolution with fewer initial candidates (small qaz/qel) to reduce memory and time.

nodes.title: Estimation Algorithm: Modified DCS-SOMP Iteration
nodes.purpose: Describe the step-by-step process of estimating ToA, 2D-AoD, and 2D-AoA using the maximum correlation criterion, residual update, and the integration of the adaptive search step within the DCS-SOMP loop.

nodes.title: Complexity Analysis: Memory Usage and Execution Time Trade-offs
nodes.purpose: Present the theoretical and empirical comparison of memory elements and execution time between standard DCS-SOMP (large grid) and Adaptive DCS-SOMP (small grid, multiple iterations), demonstrating scalability.

nodes.title: Simulation Results: Convergence and Accuracy Validation
nodes.purpose: Analyze the simulation setup (28 GHz, 64 antennas) and results showing the convergence of estimated parameters to actual values over iterations, and the superior accuracy (lower RMSE) of the adaptive method.

nodes.title: Limitations and Future Work Scope
nodes.purpose: Acknowledge constraints such as the assumption of perfect clock synchronization, single-bounce NLoS paths only, and proposed future improvements like residue update refinement and alternative antenna arrays.

coverage_notes: The argument flows from identifying the inability of prior work to handle full 3D parameter estimation efficiently (Nodes 1-2) to the proposed solution of an adaptive sensing matrix (Nodes 3-4).
Mathematical definitions for response vectors and the sensing matrix are critical for understanding the memory bottleneck addressed by the adaptive mechanism.
Simulation results explicitly validate the claim that the adaptive method achieves higher accuracy with significantly lower computational cost compared to the non-adaptive baseline.
Algorithm pseudocode (Alg 1 & 2) provides the logical bridge between the theoretical adaptive concept and the implemented solution.
